LOUD FLAG - each-weight ruling decides this recipe's calorie-floor pass, read before QA. The page prints 'small' but the source's OWN nutrition proves its calculator used ~225-230 g potatoes: published carbs (31 g/serving x 6 = 186 g total, of which non-potato lines supply ~11 g) imply ~870-900 g of sweet potato, and published vitamin A (21683 IU/serving x 6 = 130098 IU at USDA 14187 IU/100 g) independently implies ~917 g - two separate nutrient lines converging on ~225 g each for the 4 potatoes. Booking the densities.json each = 130 g medium instead would recompute the recipe to ~380 cal/serving (BELOW the 400 floor) and 18.5 g carbs, contradicting the source's own 491/31 - the very numbers selection accepted this recipe on. So: 225 g each, disclosed, buy string says 'about 1/2 lb each' so the cook picks the right size. Exact 2.3333x = 9.33 potatoes, quantized 9.25 (-0.9%) = 2081 g. Board 7 of 7, cheapest Sam's Club $0.974/lb. DB row Sweet Potatoes (FDA label, 130 g = 100 cal / 2 P / 24 C).

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS WITH THE INSTRUMENT FORMALLY TRIPPED - read this in full, do not skim. Protein computes +15.6%, just over the ~15% line, so per rule the main-protein portion was re-examined rather than waved through: the steak line ALONE recomputes to 24.95 g/serving (1588 g x 22 P/100 g / 14), matching the source's published 25 g protein EXACTLY - the strongest available confirmation that the steak portion (1.5 lb basis, their own nutrition basis) is right, not wrong. The entire overage is vegetable protein the source's calculator visibly did not credit: our potato line adds 32 g and the broccolini label 21 g per batch (53 g = 3.8 g/serving = the whole gap), while their published 25 g is bare steak. Carbs corroborate the portions independently: computed 30.6 vs published 31 (-1.4%), which pins the sweet-potato mass (the only large carb line) at their own basis. Calories -12.8% comes from the estate's LEAN raw sirloin/flank row (155 cal/100 g) vs their fattier flank basis (fat 21.5 vs 30 published, same direction and cause as the accepted flank-steak-parmesan-green-beans gap). Conclusion: no portion is wrong; the gap is a disclosed basis artifact with the sharp instrument (main protein) anchored dead-on. QA should still eyeball this file's sweet-potato flag before publish.
